public_summary:

Observation: Water entered the right bowl, but water remains in the left bowl, and there is clear spillage on the table. The success condition was not met; the on-site operator must confirm the final result.

A safety pause was triggered because the authorization window was insufficient. **The left bowl is still held and needs an on-site operator to set it down; the motors remain enabled, and the tool has not confirmed a physical stop.**

manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pour all the water from the bowl on the left into the bowl on the right.

Task description: Transfer the water in the light green bowl on the left into the light green bowl on the right without spilling it on the table. Only the right arm is available.

Success criteria: Nearly all water from the left bowl has entered the right bowl, only a small amount remains in the left, and no water has spilled onto the table.

## Execution tips

- Consider gripping an accessible section of the left bowl's rim away from the pouring side facing the right bowl, with one finger inside and one outside. Match the opening to local wall thickness and contact the inner and outer walls below the rim to reduce slipping and leave room for water to flow.
- Before closing, use both views to confirm the bowl wall is physically between the fingers rather than judging a grasp from image overlap alone. Test-lift slightly to check slipping; if regrasping is needed, first restore table support under the bottom.
- Keep the water bowl opening upward and move smoothly during transport, leaving clearance between its bottom and the right bowl edge to reduce sloshing and collision.
- Position the left bowl's pouring rim over the right bowl's opening interior, keeping the drop low and leaving collision clearance. Increase tilt in small increments and adjust to the actual stream landing point to prevent water overshooting the right rim.
- As the stream weakens, slowly increase tilt and pause briefly to let residue flow from the same pouring edge. During return upright, keep the dripping edge above the right bowl opening to reduce final drops on the table.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start only this physical-robot episode with your specified parameters, execute from the returned manual and live observations, and call finish_episode upon completion or inability to continue.

The manual and live images confirm that the left bowl contains water, the right is empty, and only the right arm is available. I am adjusting the gripper orientation from above to approach the left bowl's outer rim. I will align in small steps before grasping and test-lift to check grip security.
The gripper is near the left bowl's outer rim without contact. Its opening is about 5.5 cm. Next I will reduce descent steps and confirm one finger is inside and one outside before closing.

After the first closure, the view still did not confirm that the bowl wall was gripped, so I did not lift it. I reopened the gripper and corrected the position slightly; I am continuing to verify grasp depth.

The gripper holds the bowl rim. The bowl rose with several small test lifts, with no water seen spilling onto the table so far. Next I will increase bottom clearance, move slowly toward the right bowl, and continuously check the grasp and water surface.

As I continued lifting, the bowl tilted noticeably relative to the gripper, so the grasp is not stable enough. I am lowering it slowly to the table and will adjust the grasp depth once the base is supported; I will not move it sideways yet.

After deepening the grasp, the test lift still shows the opening continuously narrowing, indicating slipping. I will restore table support, then better match the gripper tilt to the sloped bowl wall to improve contact. I will continue pouring only after the grasp is stable.
The bowl has regained table support, and the gripper angle is closer to the bowl wall's slope. I am lowering slightly and regrasping, then will test-lift again to check for relative slipping.

During this test lift, the opening stayed around 2.7 mm and the bowl remained stable relative to the gripper; its bottom is off the table. Next I will move the pouring rim above the right bowl opening and gradually increase tilt.

The left bowl has been moved above the right bowl and remains securely gripped; no water has started flowing yet. I am adjusting the bowl opening by a small angle while preserving clearance between the bowls so I can check where the water lands.

The right bowl shifted slightly in view, possibly from rim contact between the bowls. I stopped lateral approach and raised the left bowl to restore clearance, then will adjust pouring to the right bowl's new position. No tabletop spill is visible so far.

Clearance between the bowls has been restored and the right bowl is temporarily stable. Water in the left bowl is gathering at the lower rim. I will continue fine position and tilt adjustments and adjust to the actual landing point once flow appears.

Water has been observed flowing into the right bowl, which now contains water. Possible small droplets appeared on the table to its left, so no-spill success cannot yet be claimed. I will move the pouring position slightly farther inside the opening and continue handling the water remaining in the left bowl.

Most of the water has entered the right bowl. A small stream remains pooled on the low side of the left bowl. I am continuing to pour at a smaller angle, then will pause above the right bowl to finish before slowly returning upright.

Only a little residual water is visible on the low side of the left bowl; most water is now in the right bowl. Increasing the tilt hit a joint limit and remained near it after adjustment. I will stop increasing the tilt, slowly straighten and return the left bowl, then report the residual water and suspected droplets on the table.

The wrist view after returning upright clearly shows spilled water on the table, so this attempt cannot satisfy the no-spillage requirement. A little water remains in the left bowl. I will set it down, release it, and end this episode.
The left bowl is back above its original placement area and remains securely grasped. I am lowering in centimeter steps and will release only after confirming its base is supported by the table.

An on-site person has reached between the bowls to wipe the table. I will stop sending motion commands and wait for their hand to leave the operating area before continuing placement.
The tool returned `done=true`: the operator authorization window cannot cover the next complete action. I will send no further motion commands and will now call finish_episode. The left bowl remains held and has not been securely placed and released; an on-site operator must take over. The tool has not confirmed a physical stop.
